text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first. It catches routing flaws before they hit users, proving its value without risk. The trade-off is delayed feedback for other PRs, but catching a bad route early saves more time.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on the newest open PR risks exposing *new* edge cases that could mislead reviewers or break the PR’s core function—validating PR-Agent’s routing flaws while the PR itself may still be unstable. A safer alternative: run PR-Agent in shadow mode on a *stable* PR first, then expand to newer ones once confidence is proven. Settle it by measuring false positives/negatives in shadow mode before risking live PRs.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR first to validate its stability and routing accuracy before trusting it on newer PRs—this reduces the risk of exposing edge cases in unstable code. Then, after confirming PR-Agent’s reliability, expand shadow mode to the newest open PR to catch routing flaws early without delaying feedback on other PRs.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the *oldest merged PR first*. This tests its routing and stability against proven code, not live risks. The trade-off is delayed catching of routing flaws in newer PRs, but we avoid misleading reviewers with false positives from unstable code. Once it passes on old PRs, we expand to newer ones with confidence.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR first to validate routing stability, then expand to the newest open PR once proven reliable.

Result: Shadow mode logs must show PR-Agent’s routing accuracy and no false positives on stable code, then demonstrate catching routing flaws in newer PRs without breaking PR reviews.
